positions.stance: Supports output-based telemetry and runtime auditing without static pre-market certification to prevent compliance monopolies and maintain startup competitiveness.
Supports pre-deployment safety gates and strict liability with financial capitalization floors to internalize tail risks and prevent unrecoverable harms at scale.

verdicts.conflict: Appropriate regulatory mechanisms for balancing innovation with safety incentives in autonomous software deployment
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist position accounts for catastrophic tail risks and historical precedent in complex hazardous industries, whereas the accelerationist focus on startup competitiveness overlooks systemic externalities.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical proof that post-market insurance mechanisms and runtime telemetry alone can contain catastrophic autonomous failures without imposing prohibitive public safety costs.
